cases.description: The documented "row" info_type returns the row number of the referenced cell
cases.expected_note: Excel documents info_type "row" as returning the "Row number of the cell in reference". B7 is in row 7. This is one of the four info_types this corpus tests, because it depends only on the reference itself -- see the exclusions listed on the "type" cases below

cases.description: The documented "col" info_type returns the column number of the referenced cell
cases.expected_note: Excel documents info_type "col" as returning the "Column number of the cell in reference". Column D is the 4th column

cases.description: A multi-cell reference, where the documentation says the upper-left cell is used
cases.expected_note: Excel documents that "address" returns the "Reference of the first cell in reference" and that "contents" returns the "Value of the upper-left cell in reference", so a range argument resolves to its upper-left cell. C3 is in column C, the 3rd column

cases.description: The documented "contents" info_type returns the value of the referenced cell
cases.expected_note: Excel documents info_type "contents" as returning the "Value of the upper-left cell in reference; not a formula". A1 holds the number 42

cases.description: The documented "type" info_type returns "v" for a cell holding a value
cases.expected_note: Excel documents info_type "type" as returning "'v' for value if the cell contains anything else" (that is, anything other than blank or a text constant). A1 holds the number 42

cases.description: The documented "type" info_type returns "l" for a cell holding a text constant
cases.expected_note: Excel documents "type" as returning "'l' for label if the cell contains a text constant". A2 holds the text "hello"

cases.description: The documented "type" info_type returns "b" for an empty cell
cases.expected_note: Excel documents "type" as returning "'b' for blank if the cell is empty". A3 is deliberately left unset. EXCLUSIONS: this corpus tests only the four deterministic info_types "row", "col", "contents" and "type". The others are deliberately omitted because their results are not a property of the formula: "address" and "filename" depend on the workbook's path and quoting (and "filename" is documented to return empty text for an unsaved sheet); "format", "color", "parentheses", "prefix", "protect" and "width" depend on cell formatting, column width and sheet protection that survive an .xlsx round-trip inconsistently, and Microsoft documents all six as unsupported in Excel for the web, Excel Mobile and Excel Starter; and the reference-omitted form CELL(info_type) is excluded because Microsoft's own page warns it reports "your active cell" at calculation time and "does not reliably produce information about a specific cell" -- it is volatile by design and could not be asserted against any fixed value
